hints: Focus on Group 2 trends down the group, barium is below calcium so think about how size of the cation changes both trends.
Remember hydroxides get more soluble down Group 2, so barium hydroxide solution is much more soluble than limewater.
Now link carbonate stability to cation polarising power, the smaller calcium ion distorts the carbonate ion more easily so it decomposes at a lower temperature.
walkthrough:
**Compare hydroxide solubilities**

Think of limewater versus baryta water. Solubility of Group 2 hydroxides increases down the group as the lattice energy falls faster than the hydration energy.

Trend: $$\text{Mg(OH)}_2 < \text{Ca(OH)}_2 < \text{Sr(OH)}_2 < \text{Ba(OH)}_2 \text{ (solubility increases down)}$$

**Compare carbonate thermal stabilities**

All carbonates decompose on heating in the same way. A larger cation is less polarising, so it distorts the carbonate ion less and more heat is needed.

Decomposition equation:
$$\text{MCO}_3 \rightarrow \text{MO} + \text{CO}_2$$

**Apply to calcium vs barium**

$\text{Ca}^{2+}$ is smaller than $\text{Ba}^{2+}$, so it has higher charge density and higher polarising power. That means calcium carbonate is less thermally stable and needs a lower temperature to decompose.

Conclusion: calcium hydroxide lower solubility, barium hydroxide higher solubility, calcium carbonate lower stability, barium carbonate higher stability.

options.A: Both comparisons are reversed. Calcium hydroxide is not more soluble than barium hydroxide, and calcium carbonate is not more stable than barium carbonate.
options.B: Thermal stability part is correct, but solubility is reversed. This is the common trap of thinking hydroxides become less soluble down the group like sulfates do.
options.C: Solubility part is correct, but thermal stability is reversed. Calcium carbonate decomposes more easily than barium carbonate because the smaller Ca2+ ion polarises the carbonate ion more strongly.
options.D: Correct on both trends. Hydroxide solubility increases down Group 2 so barium hydroxide is higher, and carbonate thermal stability increases down Group 2 so barium carbonate is higher.
